legend: As an entertainment after the programming contest, you hold a game event for the participants.

Two sets of cards, red ones and blue ones, are used in the game. Both of the two sets have the same number of cards as the number of the participants, and each card has one integer written on it. It is known that the contents of these two sets are the same; the integers on the red cards are the same as those on the blue cards as multisets. Even though, you don't know what integers are actually written on the cards. The same integer may be written on two or more cards of the same color, and the integers may be negative.

You distributed one red card and one blue card to each of the participants. As the game result depends on the sum of the integers on the two cards distributed to each participant, you asked all the participants to declare their sums.

Your task is to find a possible card distribution consistent with the participants' declarations, that is, a combination of integers on the cards distributed to each participant. Note that such a combination might not exist, as the participants may commit miscalculations. In such a case, report that there is no consistent combination.
input: The input consists of multiple datasets, each in the following format. The number of datasets does not exceed 100$$$100$$$.

Here, n$$$n$$$ is the number of the participants, an integer between 1$$$1$$$ and 70$$$70$$$, inclusive. Each of si$$$s_i$$$ (i=1,…,n)$$$(i = 1, \ldots, n)$$$ is the declared sum of the integers on the two cards distributed to the i$$$i$$$-th participant, an integer between −150$$$-150$$$ and 150$$$150$$$, inclusive.
The end of the input is indicated by a line consisting of a zero.
output: For each dataset, if there exists no combination of integers on the cards distributed to each participant that is consistent with the participants' declarations, output "No" in one line. Otherwise, output "Yes" in one line followed by one possible consistent combination in the following format.

Here, for i=1,…,n,$$$i = 1, \ldots, n,$$$ ai$$$a_i$$$ and bi$$$b_i$$$ represent the integers on the red and blue cards, respectively, distributed to the i$$$i$$$-th participant. Each of ai$$$a_i$$$ and bi$$$b_i$$$ must be an integer between −109$$$-10^9$$$ and 109$$$10^9$$$, inclusive. It can be proved that, when one or more consistent combinations exist, there also exists a consistent combination satisfying this condition. If there are two or more such combinations, you may output any one of them.

legend.ai: 作为编程竞赛后的娱乐活动，你为参赛者举办了一场游戏活动。
游戏中使用两组卡片，分别为红色卡片和蓝色卡片。两组卡片的数量都与参赛者人数相同，并且每张卡片上都写有一个整数。已知这两组卡片的内容相同，即红色卡片上的整数与蓝色卡片上的整数构成相同的多重集合。不过，你不知道卡片上实际写着哪些整数。同一种颜色的两张或更多卡片上可能写有相同的整数，并且这些整数可能为负数。
你给每位参赛者分发一张红色卡片和一张蓝色卡片。由于游戏结果取决于分发给每位参赛者的两张卡片上的整数之和，你要求所有参赛者报出他们的和。
你的任务是找出一种与参赛者的声明相符的可能卡片分配方案，即确定每位参赛者所分得的卡片上的整数。注意，这样的方案可能不存在，因为参赛者可能计算错误。在这种情况下，请报告不存在一致的方案。

input.ai: 输入由多个数据集组成，每个数据集的格式如下。数据集的数量不超过 100$$$100$$$。
其中，n$$$n$$$ 表示参与者的数量，是一个介于 1$$$1$$$ 和 70$$$70$$$(含)之间的整数。每个 si$$$s_i$$$(i=1,…,n)$$$(i = 1, \ldots, n)$$$ 表示分发给第 i$$$i$$$ 位参与者的两张卡片上的整数之和，是一个介于 −150$$$-150$$$ 和 150$$$150$$$(含)之间的整数。
输入以一行仅包含一个零表示结束。

output.ai: 对于每个数据集，如果不存在一种为每位参与者分配卡片上整数的方案，使其与参与者的声明一致，则输出一行 "No"。否则，输出一行 "Yes"，并按照以下格式在接下来的一行中输出一种符合条件的方案。

其中，对于 i=1,…,n，$$$i = 1, \ldots, n,$$$ ai$$$a_i$$$ 和 bi$$$b_i$$$ 分别表示分发给第 i$$$i$$$ 位参与者的红色卡片和蓝色卡片上的整数。ai$$$a_i$$$ 和 bi$$$b_i$$$ 均必须是介于 −109$$$-10^9$$$ 和 109$$$10^9$$$(含)之间的整数。可以证明，当存在一个或多个符合条件的方案时，也一定存在满足该条件的方案。如果这样的方案有两个或更多，可以输出其中任意一个。
